target.title: refactor(gateway): simplify canonical WebSocket client
target.body:
Closes #106274

## What Problem This Solves

The first Gateway WebSocket client consolidation established one lifecycle but left duplicated auth selection in the Node and Control UI adapters, plus a separate request correlator and type modules around the canonical protocol client. The relevant production surface grew to 2,943 lines after consolidation, making the architectural win hard to maintain and obscuring which layer owned requests and authentication decisions.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves shared connect-auth selection, scope reuse, auth-frame assembly, and device-token retry eligibility into one browser-safe module. It also folds request correlation and its public types into the canonical protocol lifecycle, deleting the two single-owner request/type modules. Node and browser adapters still own their environment-specific transport, device storage, trust policy, error presentation, and reconnect decisions; protocol v4 and wire frames are unchanged.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. The Control UI keeps its existing secure-WebSocket policy, reconnect timing, visible error surfaces, and automatic reconnect flow. Maintainers now have one auth decision path and one protocol/request state machine.

The follow-up is net −133 lines overall. The relevant production client surface falls from 2,943 to 2,808 lines (−135), and from 2,871 to 2,808 lines (−63) versus the two original pre-consolidation clients.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox focused Gateway/UI proof: 259 tests passed across Node client, package watchdog, Control UI client, and gateway store.
- Blacksmith Testbox full Control UI suite: 237 files / 3,769 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `check:changed`: format, production/test/UI typechecks, lint, import-cycle, and repository guards passed.
- Full repository build passed; final `@openclaw/gateway-client` package build and declarations passed.
- Real browser flow against a real loopback Gateway passed: initial connected shell, actual Gateway process stop, visible `Reconnecting…` state, new Gateway process on the same port, automatic recovery without reload/manual retry, and four browser-observed WebSocket connections.
- Fresh structured autoreview of the protocol lifecycle/request fold: no findings, patch correct, confidence 0.97. Auth adapter hunks received whole-path manual review because the review bundle's secret scanner intentionally rejects auth-token diffs.
- `git diff --check` passed.
